Definition: from G1909 and some form of the base of G4591; remarkable, i.e. (figuratively) eminent:--notable, of note.
BiblicalUsage: Episemos means notable, of note, remarkable — and the word cuts both ways. Barabbas was a notable prisoner, chosen over Jesus; and Andronicus and Junia are of note among the apostles, fellow prisoners with Paul.
TheologicalSignificance: Barabbas was notable and guilty, Andronicus and Junia were notable and faithful, and being notable is no measure of being right.
